draw.method: wiper-motor (3 groups) excluded: GROUP_HOLD_CATS in scraper/junkyard_scraper.py, never ships. 30 groups stratified by category, largest remainder; random.Random(seed).sample over sorted ids per category in sorted category order. Then 30 distinct other shippable groups, one random vehicle-year each (rng.choice over sorted (make, model, year)). Own reader; audit11_4/sample.py not used.

standard: Each item is judged from the raw product-page fitment rows and each app vehicle-year's own list-page row (Fitting Vehicle Options, Production Date), plus the lot at a85c654 replayed through a Python port of the app's OEM-GATE code (pfOemDonorGate, pfAppMatches; drive/body/cab/eng/fuel/trans verdicts line by line). WRONG: a car the app shows as a plain row cannot take the part per the raw evidence. That covers (a) a car whose own decode or listing contradicts a limit the catalog states (product-page engine column, own-page option codes), (b) a stated drive/body/cab/engine/trans/fuel limit that excludes a configuration the same catalog shows exists for that app-year, left ungated so those cars get plain rows (the earlier drive failure class), (c) an app-year no US car of which can take the number, (d) a market variant (km/h cluster) whose US counterpart has different sharing, (e) a feed model that mixes two catalog models (Rogue / Rogue Select). Trim, option-package and partial production-date limits that no decode can show are taken as carried by the group's 'fits some option packages / configurations; verify the number on the part' note, which is the design the app ships; where the catalog names the trim plainly this is recorded as an observation. RISK: the evidence for a shown row is incomplete either way, with what is missing named. Items 25 and 27 are WRONG under (b) but borderline (see their 'borderline' field).

census.scope: all 283 shippable groups (286 in the candidate; the 3 wiper-motor groups are held by GROUP_HOLD_CATS and never ship). Own parser of the Fitting Vehicle Options strings: alternatives split on top-level ', ', configurations on top-level '+', leading '*' dropped; a pn row is drive-limited when every configuration names one drive family (2WD tokens vs 4WD/AWD/AUTO) and some other row on the same page names the other family.

agree: The gates that exist read right against the raw rows: every drive (2wd/4wd/a4wd), cab, eng, fuel and trans line I saw names a limit the catalog prints, and the app port hides contradicting decodes as the section 'How the app applies it' says (4x2 decodes hidden for 4WD-only clusters, 1.6L hidden for the SR20DE speedometer, the 5.6L Pathfinder hidden for the 4.0L A/C controller).

The earlier check's two classes are largely fixed: of its census's 43 DRIVE groups, 25 are no longer in the candidate, 16 carry a drive gate and 2 are ungated, and the B14 200SX sedan rows are gone (G03/G05 removed, G06 lost 1999). The earlier RISK on Titan rear-door motors (G23 82730-9FJ0A, in my sample too) is now a crew-cab gate, which I judged RIGHT.
Overlap with the earlier verifier's items: G16/G25/G26/G28/P04/P07/P16 RIGHT in both checks.
disagree: Selfcheck census '0 unexplained suspects' and seeded sample '0 WRONG': I find 11 WRONG in 60 items. The main gap is that engine limits printed only in the product page's engine column (they follow a trim: Frontier/Xterra SE/SC 3.3L, PRO-4X/LE 4.0L, Pathfinder V8 clusters, the 2.5L-only Q40 rows) are not gated, so cars whose own decode names the other engine get plain rows (census: 20 groups, 286 lot cars).

The earlier verifier judged P14 27510-8Z315 RIGHT from an Xterra/Frontier seeker-donor pair; with the lot replayed, 3 2.4L Xterra 2002 donors are plain rows for this SE-only, 3.3L-only number (my item 3, WRONG).

The fix for the earlier P08 (QX60 2014 cluster from the gas page only) was a 'gas' fuel gate. Per the gates section that gate follows the parts table and counts as met when nothing says hybrid, so the 8 lot QX60 Hybrids (5N1CL0 VINs, decode 2.5L, listed as plain 'QX60') are still plain rows (my P38 and G12). The design choice is stated; I disagree that it is safe where the hybrid has its own displacement.
Two of the earlier census's DRIVE groups are still ungated: 24820-1MK5A and 24820-6AH2A, coded '2WDSTD' / '2WDHICAS' (joined tokens), so M37x AWD cars are plain rows.
The Pathfinder AUTO fix gates the AUTO numbers (a4wd), but the part-time '4WD' numbers of the same model-years are gated '4wd', which confirms All-Mode cars too (P43 24810-EA48D).

Not raised by either earlier report: the km/h cluster 24810-EC44C (policy.py already holds Subaru gauge clusters for this reason), and the Rogue / Rogue Select 2014-2015 mix (3 groups, 34 S35 cars each).
